source: Published aircraft figures and simple calculations from them. The model is the WING ALONE (no fuselage, tail, nacelles), so only wing-dominated coefficients are compared, all rescaled to the published reference area. Each value says whether it is published, calculated from published inputs, or an estimate.

cruiseCl.source: Calculated: 65 t at FL350, Mach 0.785, ISA, S = 124.6 m2 (range 0.48-0.51 for 60-75 t at FL310-370)

buffetOnsetCl.source: Estimate: 1.3 g buffet-margin rule x CL at the 1.3 g maximum altitude (about FL379 at 65 t, not verified); no public Boeing buffet boundary found

landingClMax.source: Rudolph, NASA CR-4746 (1996), Fig. 2.29: 737-X approach CL 1.75 x 1.54 (CLmax / CL_approach, p. 40); 737-300: 2.75

dragDivergenceMach.source: Proxy: published typical cruise Mach 0.785 (airliners cruise at about M_dd); no published M_dd. MMO 0.82.

cruiseCl.source: Calculated: 330 t at FL350, Mach 0.855, ISA, S = 525 m2 (range 0.48-0.51 for 270-380 t at FL310-390)

buffetOnsetCl.source: Estimate: 1.3 g buffet-margin rule x CL at the 1.3 g maximum altitude (about FL370 at 330 t, not verified); no public Boeing buffet boundary found

landingClMax.source: Rudolph, NASA CR-4746 (1996), Fig. 2.29: 747-400 approach CL 1.36 x 1.54 (CLmax / CL_approach, p. 40); approach 146 kt at MLW (p. 79)

dragDivergenceMach.source: Proxy: published cruise Mach 0.855 (Wikipedia, citing Boeing); no published M_dd. MMO 0.92.

citations: R. K. Rudolph, 'High-Lift Systems on Commercial Subsonic Airliners', NASA CR-4746, 1996. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19960052267
